title: The Pentagon Wants to Use AI to Kill People Without Checks. Is Anthropic Really Pushing Back?
author: Taylor Lorenz
content:
[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!8K4t!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-
post-

post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fc2f47166-12b1-4782-b9ad-3b57c0e32669_6048x4024.jpeg)_Photo
illustration by Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto via Getty Images_

Over the weekend, the US military relied on Anthropic's powerful AI model,
Claude,[ to help support the launch](https://www.axios.com/newsletters/axios-
am-f0954cb2-2f31-4426-87fd-050095005344.html?chunk=2&utm_term=twsocialshare#story2)
of its brutal attack on Iran. The Pentagon used Claude despite the fact that
just hours earlier, the Trump administration declared it would end use of
Anthropic's AI tools after a spat over the government's desire to mass-surveil
US citizens using its AI model.

The dispute between Anthropic and the US government has devolved into a
chaotic split that has upended Silicon Valley, thrown the government into
confusion, and kicked off a national debate about the ethics of AI in warfare.

The controversy over Claude began last summer, when the Pentagon
[awarded](https://www.defenseone.com/defense-systems/2025/07/pentagon-awards-
multiple-companies-200m-contracts-ai-tools/406700/) Anthropic, Google, OpenAI,
and Elon Musk's xAI government contracts worth up to $200 million each to
develop AI systems for the military and for use in "national security."
Anthropic was the first to obtain government clearance for use in classified
settings. Two former OpenAI executives, Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei, along
with a handful of other former OpenAI employees who [didn't like where OpenAI
was going](https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/dario-amodei-sam-altman-better-to-
follow-your-own-vision-anthropic-co-founder-on-leaving-openai-11129566),
founded Anthropic in 2021.

The government deemed that Anthropic's model was the most advanced and secure
system for sensitive military operations, but the contract was not without
stipulations. Anthropic said that Claude AI could not be used for fully
autonomous weapons or mass domestic surveillance, two things that the company
has claimed to stand against.

### **Bright Lines and Supply Chains**

But after the US military's raid on Venezuela in early January 2026, questions
began to arise about how the government was actually using Anthropic's tech.
After Anthropic discovered that its AI model, Claude, was used in the raid via
the company's partnership with Palantir, executives at Anthropic [became
uncomfortable](https://thehill.com/policy/defense/5744403-anthropic-pentagon-
ai-dispute/).

The company wanted to be sure that the government was honoring its commitment
not to employ Claude for autonomous weapons or mass domestic surveillance.
Once the military learned Anthropic wasn't happy, it reacted.

The Pentagon announced that it would [review its relationship with
Anthropic](https://thehill.com/policy/defense/5740369-pentagon-anthropic-
relationship-review/) in light of the dispute over the usage policy, and that
set off tense, weeks-long back-and-forth negotiations between Anthropic and
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Hegseth has been adamant that Anthropic, as a government contractor, must
allow its technology to be used, effectively, in any way the military sees
fit. Dario Amodei has responded by drawing a bright line at autonomous weapons
and mass domestic surveillance, and refused to capitulate. The crux of the
dispute centered on the Pentagon's desire to use Anthropic's AI to bulk
analyze large swaths of commercially-obtained data collected about Americans
for mass surveillance, according to [a
report](https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/2026/03/inside-anthropics-
killer-robot-dispute-with-the-
pentagon/686200/?gift=2iIN4YrefPjuvZ5d2Kh30zpPxOtZj8TuGGLnTN11Z-s) by _The
Atlantic_.

[Share](https://zeteo.com/p/anthropic-pentagon-ai-military-
openai?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&action=share&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjozNjIwMjc3ODksInBvc3RfaWQiOjE4OTc3MTgwOSwiaWF0IjoxNzcyNjQ1NDU1LCJleHAiOjE3NzUyMzc0NTUsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0yMzI1NTExIiwic3ViIjoicG9zdC1yZWFjdGlvbiJ9.Vw2A3om9TDveiLDpmEGfFYGaBKqDb0DBC3g49FhW8ek)

Last Friday, things reached a breaking point when it became clear that
Anthropic wouldn't budge. In response, Trump ordered the federal government to
cease all use of Anthropic's technology. "I am directing EVERY Federal Agency
in the United States Government to IMMEDIATELY CEASE all use of Anthropic's
technology. We don't need it, we don't want it, and will not do business with
them again!" he posted [to Truth
Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/116144552969293195).

Hegseth also said he planned to declare Anthropic a "supply chain risk,"
meaning that the AI company would be placed under major restrictions governing
its business relationships. Companies declared "supply chain risks" usually
only include firms like Huawei, a Chinese-based tech company, where the
technology itself could be used by a foreign government for espionage.

The supply chain risk designation means that all government contractors and
even subcontractors like Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Raytheon, or any of the
thousands of private companies that do business with the Pentagon must cut
ties with Anthropic or risk losing their own government contracts. This has
led to confusion as companies across the country scramble to figure out how
they'll navigate this split.

In the meantime, OpenAI swooped in. CEO Sam Altman announced on Friday that
the company had signed a deal allowing its AI model to be used by the
military's classified systems. Because the exact terms of the contract are not
public, however, it's unclear whether Altman compromised on the guardrails on
which Amodei insisted.

Altman has tweeted the announcement three separate times, [two
of](https://x.com/sama/status/2028640354912923739)
[which](https://x.com/sama/status/2027578508042723599) bear a community note
saying that, "Government officials have contradicted Sam's claim, saying
OpenAI will allow the DoW to use their models for 'all lawful purposes.' This
could allow for uses Anthropic refused to engage in, namely mass surveillance
tools and weapons systems with no human oversight." On Monday, Altman tweeted
again, attempting to clarify the contract further but ultimately [raising many
of the same questions](https://x.com/tysonbrody/status/2028655003468980675).

### **A Marketing Opportunity**

While a slew of Silicon Valley leaders [and
investors](https://x.com/Jason/status/2027518386641449400), like [Palmer
Luckey](https://x.com/PalmerLuckey/status/2027500334999081294), staffers at
venture firm [Andreessen Horowitz](https://www.businessinsider.com/marc-
andreessen-ben-horowitz-donated-millions-pro-trump-pac-2024-10), and venture
capitalist [Keith
Rabois](https://www.scmp.com/magazines/style/entertainment/article/3304279/meet-
silicons-valleys-trump-whisperer-jacob-helberg-presidents-under-secretary-
economic-growth), have offered support for the Trump admin, much of the public
is on Anthropic's side.

On Saturday morning, Anthropic's Claude AI app [shot to the
top](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/02/28/anthropics-claude-apple-apps.html) of
Apple's app store. The sidewalk in front of Anthropic's San Francisco office
is [covered in chalk-written messages from
supporters](https://missionlocal.org/2026/02/sf-anthropic-pete-hegsteth-trump-
sidewalk-chalk/). Pop star Katy Perry [posted a
screenshot](https://x.com/katyperry/status/2027619173325553765) of herself
purchasing a Claude pro-plan with a big heart drawn on top.

Amodei is undeniably right to stand up to the government's unethical demands
to exert control over their technology. But as many have also correctly
pointed out, this is also a massive [marketing
opportunity](https://www.usnews.com/news/technology/articles/2026-02-28/what-
to-know-about-the-clash-between-the-pentagon-and-anthropic-over-militarys-ai-
use) for Anthropic.

Amodei speaks onstage during the New York Times DealBook Summit 2025 on Dec.

Consumers are rapidly turning against Big Tech as the effects of AI are felt
more and more in our daily lives. Amodei has
[predicted](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/27/dario-amodei-warns-ai-cause-
unusually-painful-disruption-jobs.html) that AI could eliminate up to half of
all entry-level white-collar jobs within five years, and it makes sense for
him to position Anthropic as the good guys in this technological shift.

Timnit Gebru, a computer scientist and sharp critic of the AI industry, who
formerly co-led Google's ethical artificial intelligence team,
[posted](https://x.com/timnitGebru/status/2027579669277774234) that she has
"nothing good to say about Anthropic" just like she had nothing good to say
about Musk in his feud with Trump.

"Anthropic knowingly partnered with the pentagon [sic]," she
[said](https://x.com/timnitGebru/status/2027579669277774234) on X. "Their
other partner, Palantir, is probably the most evil [sic] tech company in the
world, which, among other things, powers the ICE abductions of members of our
communities… I have zero good things to say about them. If I hated OpenAI more
than Google, I hate Anthropic more than OpenAI."

Gebru also [urged the
public](https://x.com/timnitGebru/status/2027784516186869816) not to "fall for
the theatrics."

### **Bellwether Moment**

Still, this could be a bellwether moment for Silicon Valley, where, hopefully,
tech companies begin to think more critically about the ways their AI products
are used. It could also result in other Silicon Valley startups refusing to
enable the US war machine.

"Moral of this story is that no smart company is going to do business with
this government," one user
[tweeted](https://x.com/Afinetheorem/status/2027512879897886920). "Anthropic
built literally the world's best AI and integrated with the military, as a
national service. They fulfilled their contract precisely. Result: they are
being treated like Huawei."

[Share](https://zeteo.com/p/anthropic-pentagon-ai-military-
openai?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&action=share&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjozNjIwMjc3ODksInBvc3RfaWQiOjE4OTc3MTgwOSwiaWF0IjoxNzcyNjQ1NDU1LCJleHAiOjE3NzUyMzc0NTUsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0yMzI1NTExIiwic3ViIjoicG9zdC1yZWFjdGlvbiJ9.Vw2A3om9TDveiLDpmEGfFYGaBKqDb0DBC3g49FhW8ek)

"Today's 'boycott ChatGPT" vibe feels a lot like #DeleteUber in 2017," tech
commentator Joanna Stern
[tweeted](https://x.com/JoannaStern/status/2027825561909805394). "Real anger,
specifically at a founder, and loud exits to competition. The big difference?
This isn't a two-car race. Gemini and Claude were already gaining share, and
moments like this just accelerate switching."

For Silicon Valley to grow a moral backbone, however, startup and big tech
executives will have to sacrifice profits, something that past generations of
tech leaders have simply refused to do.

Amodei may be willing to stand up to the government when it's broadly popular
to do so, much the way that Tim Cook [defended civil
liberties](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2016/feb/22/tim-cook-apple-
refusal-unlock-iphone-fbi-civil-liberties) in 2016 when he refused to unlock
the iPhone for the FBI. However, there are myriad factors that could pressure
him to change that stance, which will become harder to defend if profits
slide.
